title: React Server vs Client Components: Quick Revision
summary: Revision notes on RSC vs Client Components: the mental model, the 'use client' boundary, props across it, composition patterns, what runs where and bundle impact.

chapters.title: Server vs Client Components: Mental Model
points: Server Components are the default in the App Router: they render only on the server, ship no component JS to the browser, and can be async and await data directly
Client Components opt in with 'use client' and render on the server for the initial HTML, then hydrate in the browser to become interactive
Server can: async/await, read DB/secrets/filesystem, use server-only code. Client can: useState/useEffect, event handlers, browser APIs (window, localStorage), context
Comparison rule: needs state, effects, onClick or browser APIs = Client; just fetches and displays data = Server
Mistake: thinking 'client' means 'browser-only'. Client Components are still pre-rendered on the server; only Server Components never hydrate

chapters.title: The 'use client' Boundary
points: 'use client' must be the first line of the file, above imports; it marks a boundary entry point, not a single component
Everything imported by a 'use client' file joins the client bundle, so you don't add the directive to each child
Server Components can import Client Components, but a Client Component cannot import a Server Component: the import would make it client code
Hooks (useState, useEffect) or event handlers in a file without 'use client' throw a build error: 'You're importing a component that needs useState'
Mistake: putting 'use client' on a layout or page 'to make it work' pulls the whole subtree into the bundle; push it down to small leaf components

chapters.title: Passing Props Across the Boundary
points: Props from Server to Client Components must be serializable: strings, numbers, booleans, plain objects/arrays, Date, Map/Set, Promises, JSX elements
Functions, class instances and event handlers cannot be passed as props; the exception is Server Actions marked 'use server'
Example: <Counter initial={await getCount()} /> works; <Button onClick={() => save()} /> from a Server Component errors
Props sent to a Client Component are included in the RSC payload and visible in the browser, so never pass secrets or whole DB rows; pass only the fields needed
Mistake: passing a non-serializable value (function, class instance), which gives 'Only plain objects can be passed to Client Components'

chapters.title: Composition Patterns
points: Children pattern: a Client Component takes children, and a Server Component passes server-rendered JSX into it: <ClientShell><ServerList /></ClientShell>; the Server child stays on the server
Slots via props: pass Server Components as props like sidebar={<ServerSidebar />}; any JSX prop works the same way as children
Context providers must be Client Components; wrap them in a providers.tsx with 'use client' and render {children} so the layout stays a Server Component
Keep interactivity in small leaves: make only the LikeButton a Client Component and leave the surrounding card as a Server Component
Mistake: importing a Server Component inside a Client file, which turns it into client code; pass it as children instead

chapters.title: What Runs Where and Bundle Impact
points: Request flow: the server renders the Server Component tree into an RSC payload (streamed), with Client Components as references; the browser merges that into the DOM, then hydrates only the client parts
Server Component code and its dependencies (e.g. a markdown or date library) never reach the browser, so they cost zero client JS
Client Components and everything they import count toward the bundle, so a heavy library imported there inflates it; keep heavy libs in Server Components
Add import 'server-only' to modules with secrets or DB access so that importing them into a Client Component fails the build; use 'client-only' for browser-only code
Mistake: reading process.env secrets in a Client Component; only NEXT_PUBLIC_ variables are inlined into the browser bundle, others are undefined

chapters.title: RSC vs Client Cheat Sheet
points: Default: Server. Add 'use client' only for state, effects, event handlers, browser APIs, or hook-based libraries
'use client' goes at the top of the file and marks a boundary; push it down to leaves
Server imports Client = OK; Client imports Server = NO, pass it as children or props
Props across the boundary must be serializable; no functions except Server Actions; never pass secrets
Providers: 'use client' wrapper taking children; guard with server-only/client-only; check bundle size with next build output or the bundle analyzer
